candidatePledges.paraphrase: Rejoin the Paris Agreement after the 2020 election.
candidatePledges.locator: Climate Change; paragraph beginning 'Democrats recognize that the United States does not stand alone'
candidatePledges.criterion: Treaty acceptance deposited and entry into force for the US during the 2021-2025 administration; later withdrawal tracked separately as durability.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: Re-entry and subsequent withdrawal are independently documented, but formal party pledge fulfillment, party-vs-president attribution and policy durability require separate coding; rejoining does not demonstrate emissions reductions or Paris target attainment.
competingExplanations: Executive treaty-acceptance authority enabled rapid action without a new statute.
Withdrawal under a subsequent administration reflects executive policy reversal, not proof of original campaign intent.

candidatePledges.paraphrase: Make permanent the 2017 tax-law increase in the federal standard deduction.
candidatePledges.locator: Chapter 3, item 2, sentence on provisions that doubled the standard deduction
candidatePledges.criterion: Remove statutory 2025 sunset for increased standard deduction; distinguish enactment, effective tax year, claimant benefit and other tax-base changes.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: Public Law 119-21 §70102 removes the sunset and increases amounts, with specified amendments applicable for tax years beginning after 2024. Does not establish every filer receives net tax relief.
competingExplanations: Legislative majority and reconciliation process were necessary for enactment.
Other simultaneous tax provisions affect net household liabilities.

candidatePledges.paraphrase: Make permanent the 2017 expansion of the federal Child Tax Credit.
candidatePledges.locator: Chapter 3, item 2, same sentence on expanded Child Tax Credit
candidatePledges.criterion: Remove statutory sunset of expanded child tax credit; separately record changed credit amount, eligibility, refundability, take-up and distribution.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: §70104 removes sunset and raises nominal amount from $2,000 to $2,200, but adds taxpayer SSN restrictions and other conditions; eligibility and net realized credits are not established.
competingExplanations: Legislative changes combine expansion with restrictions.
A nominal maximum credit is not realized average tax relief.

officialEvents.locator: DCPD202100049, Statement on Acceptance; UN treaty status cites depositary notification C.N.10.2021
officialEvents.fact: President Biden signed acceptance of the Paris Agreement on January 20, 2021; the UN records instrument deposit on that date.

officialEvents.locator: Department of State press statement dated February 19, 2021; UN Paris Agreement treaty status
officialEvents.fact: United States officially became a party again on February 19, 2021.
Order directed notice of withdrawal; not itself the treaty-effective withdrawal date.
UN depositary records withdrawal notification received January 27, 2025; treaty withdrawal effective one year later.

officialEvents.locator: United States treaty status footnote 7 and UN notice C.N.71.2025
officialEvents.fact: UN treaty status reports US withdrawal took effect January 27, 2026.
Removed end-2025 sunset of increased standard deduction and raised amounts; §70102 changes apply for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.
Removed end-2025 expanded CTC sunset, raised stated amount $2,000 to $2,200, changed SSN requirements; §70104 changes apply for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

fiscalActualObservations.electionContext: US presidential election 2020-11-03 within reporting month

fiscalProvenance.publication: January 2021 Monthly Treasury Statement, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
fiscalProvenance.reportingBasis: Federal on- and off-budget modified cash basis, not general-government accrual GFCF
fiscalProvenance.caution: Not investment or capital outlays. January 2021 report flags payment-date accelerations into December 2020 and $139bn January 2021 Economic Impact Payments. COVID fiscal response and seasonality confound election-time comparisons; no causal analysis.

coverageAndRights.campaignCorpus: Only selected clauses from two already indexed party platforms; source census and exclusions incomplete
coverageAndRights.rights: Campaign material paraphrased with locators; no bulk party text or copyrighted third-party tracker reproduced. US federal and UN primary links retained; check UN reuse terms before republication.
coverageAndRights.primarySourceLinkCheck: Individual source pages examined; not a complete automated link audit.

limitations: The three selected clauses are not a complete denominator; 2024 GOP atomic children refine an existing broad candidate and must not be double counted.
Paris reentry during Biden's term and subsequent Trump withdrawal must be evaluated at separate time horizons, not collapsed into a single binary.
The two 2025 tax statutory provisions map to one previously indexed statute; these are provision-level evidence records, not two new laws.
No independent human coding, estimated causal effects, household tax incidence or fiscal election-cycle regression.
The 2020 election-period MTS figures include pandemic response, payment-timing shifts, seasonality and a fiscal-year boundary.
